lawyer:
Mahbubur Rahman, Senior Advocate with Shafiul Alom, Advocates—For the Accused-petitioner. 
Md Fazlur Rahman Khan, DAG with Md Shafiquel Islam Siddique, DAG with Md Jahirul Islam, AAG and Md Shafiquzzaman, AAG—For the State-opposite-party.
parties:
Kazi Mahbubur Rahman ---- Accused-petitioner
vs
State ----- Opposite party
full_judgment:
AKM Abdul Hakim, J: This application for Bail under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure having been moved on behalf of Kazi Mahbubur Rahman accused in Uttara Purbo Police Station Case No. 42 dated 29-4-2018 corresponding to GR Case No. 146 of 2018 under sections 25B(1) (a) (b), 25B (2) and 25D of the Special Powers Act, 1974, now pending in the court of learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka, a rule was issued by this court on 25-5-2019 calling upon the opposite-party to show cause as to why the accused-petitioner shall not be released on bail in the aforesaid case. 

 2. The case of the prosecution, in short, is that on 29-4-2018 at about 21-30 hours, one Md Zulhas Miah, Police Inspector, CPC-1, RAB-1, Uttara, Dhaka as an informant lodged the First Information Report with Uttara Purbo Police Station against the accused-petitioner and others alleging offence under section 25B(1)(a)(b)/25B(2)/25D of the Special Powers Act, 1974 stating, inter alia, that the informant along with his companion forces were on petrol duty in connection with RAB-1, Uttara, Dhaka MCC No. 490 of 2018 dated 28-4-2018 and while the informant party staying at Gulshan-2 Area, Dhaka they received a secret information at about 16-00 hours that some international gold smugglers with illegal gold staying at Flat No. 8, 9, House No. 12, Road No. 11, Sector No. 06, Uttara, Dhaka. The informant immediately informed the matter to his higher authority and reached to the place of occurrence at about 17-10 hours, raided level A/8 Flat and arrested the accused-petitioner and others from the aforesaid flats and that it is further alleged that after searching in the aforesaid flats the informant party recovered 135 gold bars measuring about 13.495 Kgs valued at Taka 5, 00, 00,000 from bed room of Flat No. A/8 of Mahbubur Rahman, same was contained in a black colour trolley bag lying on the bed in presence of the witnesses. The accused persons could not show any valid documents regarding these gold bars. It is further alleged that on interrogation the arrested accused persons disclosed that along with their accomplices they are smuggling gold for about 05 years and that they kept the alleged recovered gold bars in the aforesaid flats for sale. Thereafter the informant party seized those gold bars by preparing a seizure-list in presence of the witness and lodged the First Information Report. 

 4. That after submissions the police report the case record was transmitted to the Metropolitan Special Tribunal No. 1 for holding trial, same was registered on 13-11-2019 as Special Tribunal Case No. 808 of 2019. Thereafter case was transferred to the Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Court No. 14 by order dated 13-11-2019, who received the case record on 20-11-2019 and after fixing so many dates for charge hearing and next date is now fixed on 11-1-2021 for charge hearing. 

 5. It is the case of the petitioner that he was arrested on 29-4-2018, then filed a petition for bail before the learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka same was rejected on 6-1-2019. Then a petition for bail was moved before the learned Metropolitan Special Tribunal No. 1, Dhaka, who by order dated 12-3-2019 rejected the prayer for bail. 

 6. Mr Mahbubur Rahman, learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that all 7 (seven) raiding party members, who are police and members of RAB in their statements under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure stated that gold was recovered from Flat No. A/7 but in FIR place of recovery was stated from Flat No. A/8 belongs to accused No. 1, Kazi Mahbubur Rahman but in fact he is not owner and not having exclusive possession and control over the alleged place of recovery, whereas the accused-petitioner resides in Flat No. A/9, which is his residence. He further submits that under section 25B(2) of Special Powers Act in which maximum punishment was 7 (seven) years imprisonment and minimum punishment is 1 (one) year. This accused-petitioner is languishing in the jail since his arrest on 28-4-2018, which is more than 2 years, 6 months and till today no charge was framed in this case and the case is now fixed on 11-1-2021 for charge hearing and this is highly derogatory to the principles of criminal justice and the fundamental rights as guaranteed and enshrined under Article 35(3) of our constitution and further there is no immediate prospect of trial of the cases and, as such, the petitioner may kindly be enlarged on bail for ends of justice due to inordinate and unreasonable delay in the trial. He next submits that out of 4 accuseds person in the present case, two accused persons namely. Md Mahbubul Alam and Tahidul Islam Touhid was granted bail by this Hon'ble court on 26-2-2019 in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 65364 of 2019 in which Rule was made absolute. Against the judgment and order dated 26-2-2019, the opposite party preferred Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 938 of 2019 in the Appellate Division and same was dismissed on 20-7-2020 and judgment and order of High Court Division allowing bail to the accused persons was upheld. The learned Advocate prays that this petitioner stand on better footing for consideration for granting bail, same privilege be extended to the accused-petitioner. He also submits that in spite of repeated police remand and brutal police torture both physically and mentally, he did not make any confessional statement under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. There is gross discrepancies and contradictions in the case which made the whole case highly doubtful. The learned Advocate lastly submits that inordinate and unreasonable delay in the trial has been found to be a good ground for enlarging the accused on bail even in a case of murder and the same principle equally apply in a case under the Special Powers Act. 

 7. Mr Fazlur Rahman Khan, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing for the state opposes the submissions advanced by the learned Advocate for the petitioner. He submits that this is a gold smuggling case and offence of the petitioner are serious in nature. He further submits that the petitioner had control, knowledge and possession of the incriminating articles. He next submits that offence will attract section 25B (1)(b) of the Special Powers Act, 1974. He also submits that in the First Information Report place of occurrence is flat no. A/8 which was corroborated by 5 (five) other persons who are flat owners, Darwans and Care-taker of the building and, as such, the accused-Petitioner should not be enlarged on bail. He lastly submits that the accused-petitioner is not stand on same footing, like other two accused-petitioners, who were granted bail. 

 8. The basic idea of bail is release of a person from the custody of police and to deliver him into the hand of surety, who undertakes to produce him in court whenever ordered to do so and in the case of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life the mere heinousness/grievousness of the offence is not by itself circumstance sufficient to take away the discretion of a court to grant bail in deprivation of the accused's fundamental right to be freed but in addition there to there must also exist reasonable grounds for believing that the person seeking bail has been guilty of such an offence. 

 9. Thus the discretion to enlarge bail has to be exercised in judicial manner with due regard to the circumstances of each case, without any tendency of unnecessary affecting the liberty of persons accused of criminal case. 

 10. It has been pointed out in the case of Manzoor vs The State, reported in PLD 1972 (SC) 81 that; 

 "Bail is not to be withheld as a punishment. There is no legal or moral compulsion to keep people in jail merely on the allegation that they have committed offences punishable with death or transportation, unless reasonable grounds appear to exist to disclose, their complicity. The ultimate conviction and incarceration of a guilty person can repair the wrong caused by a mistaken relief of interim bail granted to him, but no satisfactory preparation can be offered to an innocent man for his unjustified incarceration at any stage of the case albeit his acquittal in the long run." 

 11. In the case of Ashraf Ali Mondal vs State, reported in 1988 BLD (AD) 21 = 42 DLR (AD) 8, the prayer for bail was allowed when it was found that it was reasonable to grant bail and there is apprehension that the case may be further delayed and the appellant will suffer due to prolonged custody. 

 12. It is apparent, apart from the provision in section 339C(4) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, inordinate delay in prosecution of the present case, thereby dragging of the proceeding in a trial, for no fault of the accused may be considered to be a ground for enlarging the accused-petitioner on bail. 

 13. Section 29 of the Special Powers Act, 1974 makes the Code of Criminal Procedure applicable to the proceedings of Special Tribunal. The time limit imposed by section 339C of the Code of Criminal Procedure will also apply to the proceedings of Special Tribunal. In this connection, the decision in the case of Kamruzzaman vs The State reported in 42 DLR (AD) 219 = 1990 BLD (AD) 190 may be referred to wherein it was clearly held-Applicability of the Code to proceedings before Special Tribunals: The Act provides that the provisions of the Code shall apply to a case under the Act if they are not inconsistent with its own provisions. Section 339C of the Code being not inconsistent with any provisions of the Act shall apply to the proceedings before Special Tribunals constituted under the Act. Section 339C is intended for expeditious trial; the special statue is intended for "more speedy trial." If the provision for speedy trial is not applied to trial under the Act, it will bring a situation not intended by the lawmakers. 

 15. It is needless to repeat the principle of the Criminal Jurisprudence that 'an accused is presumed to be innocent unless contrary is proved' and in respect of an accused with allegations of commission of a non-bailable offence. We can place reliance in the case of Riasat Ali vs Ghulam Muhammad reported in 20 DLR (SC) 339. 

 16. We have carefully perused the FIR, the charge-sheet and the other materials placed before us. We do not find any material so as to distinguish the case of the accused-petitioner with those of the others who have been released on bail. Since the charge-sheet has been already submitted but charge not yet framed, we also do not find much force in the submission of the Deputy Attorney-General that the accused-petitioner, if be released, on bail, there will be scope for tampering with the evidence. 

 17. In the present case, it appears that the accused-petitioner has been languishing in the Jail hajat without trial for more than 2(two) years, 6 (six) months. We like to point out that the long delay in holding the trial and the apprehension expressed by the learned counsel for the accused-petitioner that the trial may be further delayed for one reason or the other seems to be reasonable, the petitioner ought to have been granted bail. We are of the opinion that there is much force in the contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioner regarding bail on the ground of unreasonable or inordinate delay in the trial of the case. 

 18. We have considered the above submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner and have noticed the principles laid down in the above decisions. We are satisfied that it is a fit case in which accused-petitioner should be enlarged on bail. 

 19. Having regard to our above discussion and facts and circumstances of the case, we are inclined to enlarge the accused-petitioner on bail till disposal of the Special Tribunal Case No. 808 of 2019 pending in the Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Court No. 14, Dhaka. The trial court, however, may cancel the bail on any tested ground as to misuse of bail as it may deem fit and proper.
